text.p: The first share issue by a Tibet-based company is a historical breakthrough, with the mineral water it produces able to challenge world-famous brands and help combat cancer, its underwriter said on Tuesday.

Tibet Shendi Corp plans to raise 57 million yuan from the issue of 15 million A shares this week on the Shanghai stock exchange. The group runs a hotel and tourism company and produces three brands of mineral water in the regional capital of Lhasa.

"The share issue is a symbol of Tibet's political stability, economic development and unity among the races," the Sichuan Provincial Trust & Investment Company said in a notice in Tuesday's Shanghai Securities News.
It described the issue as a milestone in the historical development of Tibet's economy and said it had attracted the attention of securities brokerages and domestic and foreign media.
An analyst at a foreign brokerage said that the issue was a breakthrough in so far as it could open up a source of capital for Tibetan companies other than central government subsidies.
"With good marketing and advertising, this mineral water could be sold abroad," he said. "Foreigners feel that Tibet is a special place. Most Chinese regard it as just poor and backward.
"If it was an appropriate industry, we could do a (foreign currency) B share issue of a Tibetan company," he said, citing the success of B share Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Product

The water used in Shendi's mineral water comes from a spring 400 metres below the ground at a site just north of the Potala Palace in Lhasa, the holiest place in Tibetan Buddhism and the former home of the Dalai Lama.
The notice said that the water had no trace of pollution, had excellent medical and health qualities, with minerals good for fighting cancer.
Annual demand for mineral water in China was nearly 40 million tonnes, with the market monopolised by foreign brands, the notice said.
Shendi had the ability to challenge these foreign brands on the domestic market and enter export markets, it said.

Brokers have forecast a good market reception for the shares because the Shanghai A share market has been on a bull run since April and the success of previous stocks issued by firms from China's minority areas.
